newsitem.title: PERU: Red Cross signals more releases imminent in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross signals more releases imminent in Peru.

text.p: The Red Cross' chief representative in Peru, Michel Minnig, indicated Wednesday that the release of more hostages from the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence was imminent.
When asked by journalists if Marxist guerrillas were about to free more of their remaining 81 captives, Minnig nodded his head in agreement.
A bus similar to those used for previous releases also pulled up outside the residence.
Minnig was communicating with journalists as he left the residence. Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani, overseeing mediations in the crisis, remained inside the building.
The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) was holding its captives for the 15th day of the crisis since it stormed the residence during a cocktail party, originally taking more than 500 hostages.
